the K‐ACT framework is a useful tool to evaluate e‐government portals.
the K‐ACT evaluation model can be applied to evaluate the KM mechanisms in e‐government portal.

(i) e‐government portals are knowledge‐based, (ii) KM mechanisms are necessary for the success of e‐government, (iii) KM mechanisms are implemented in the portals, but (iv) the implementation of the KM mechanisms is not complete.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the KM mechanisms of e‐government portal.
the evaluation of knowledge management mechanisms in e‐government websites, with the goal of providing a better understanding of how these portals can be improved.
the design of e-government portals to facilitate the access, creation, and transfer of knowledge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the knowledge access, creation, and transfer (KACT) model provides an effective and efficient framework for evaluating knowledge management in e-government portals, and that it is the first of its kind.
the paper has presented a model that is useful to the evaluation of e-government portals from the perspective of knowledge access, creation, and transfer.
knowledge management is a process that can be used in e-Government to improve the efficiency and quality of services, and to increase the effectiveness of the organization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a model for knowledge management in e-government portals and have evaluated the model using a case study.
we have developed a model for evaluating e-government portals based on knowledge management.
we developed an evaluation model for e-government portals, which is based on three main KM mechanisms, namely knowledge access, creation, and transfer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
KM is an important consideration for the success of e-government portals and the K‐ACT model provides a useful framework for evaluating their KM capabilities.
KM mechanisms are necessary for e‐government portals in order to support the access and creation of knowledge and the transfer of knowledge to users.
knowledge access, creation, and transfer are important mechanisms for e-government portals and that the dimensions of each mechanism are important for their effective implementation.
